verdict.rationale: Only generic marketing exists ('Intel Xe Media Engine delivers sharp, high-def video' while gaming/streaming) with no documented list of specific codecs (AV1/HEVC/ProRes-class) or encode/decode specs tied to the 285K SKU; the official spec page for this exact SKU lists cache, clock, AI frameworks, ECC, vPro but no media-engine codec table. Much of the marketing copy cited (battery life, 'on-the-go') appears to be generic Core Ultra brand copy not specific to this desktop K-series chip, undermining confidence it reflects 285K's actual media engine. missing for 10: SKU-specific media engine spec sheet naming AV1/HEVC/ProRes hardware encode-decode support, independent benchmark/hands-on confirmation of encode/decode performance.
